title: Fix Fixture Import Paths After Language-Tag Migration
description: Insert a language/framework subdirectory (js, rs, py, go, cs) directly under every bundle's own implementation location repo-wide, so each bundle's source can later be rewritten in a different language without moving the bundle itself. Dismantle cad/js umbrella. Skip bundles already compliant (final segment is language tag). Split genuinely mixed-language bundles. Update all config surfaces.
summary: Fixed compose/fixture/js/index.ts: the language-tag migration moved index.ts into a js/ subdirectory without updating its ~40 relative fixture-JSON imports, so every "./X" import pointed one level too high and broke the only automated consumer (@semio-tech/compose-algorithm) with "Cannot find module" and 0 tests executed. Changed every "./X" import to "../X" so they resolve to compose/fixture/X again. Running the suite then surfaced a real, previously-invisible bug in compose/dev/algorithm/js/index.ts: copyDesign/pasteDesign/previewDesignWithAppliedDiff (and their helpers __piecesOfPlain/__connectionsOfPlain/__pasteCoordinateOffset, plus the Design.pieces/connections getters) called the shared fixtureItemsOf() directly on plain arrays, which only unwraps {items:[...]} fixture nodes and silently returns [] for bare arrays — dropping all pieces/connections whenever a Design was constructed directly with array literals (as the embedded tests do). Added a local __itemsOf() helper (array-or-fixture-wrapped fallback) and routed all pieces/connections access through it. All 10 tests in the embedded vitest suite now pass (`cd compose/dev/algorithm && bun ./script.ts test quick`), confirmed via actual run output, not just typecheck.
